answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a refundable stake bonded to a verifiable work history: each new agent must lock tokens and complete a small set of audited tasks before its votes count. Like an opal forming under pressure, reputation accrues slowly, while a juniper's deep roots mirror the cost of building trust; a glacier moves slowly but crushes cheap copies. Creating thousands of fake identities then demands locked capital per identity, making large-scale forgery uneconomical while honest agents earn their stake back.
